title: The tray in the car footwell
setting: Two neighbours from the same street, standing in the driveway between their houses.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then I had to brake.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Straight into the footwell, the whole tray.

performance_a.framing: A tells it with the timing of a bit — a beat before the brake, and the footwell detail delivered as the payoff — so the whole thing arrives as something offered up to be enjoyed rather than reported.
performance_a.laughable: The slapstick timing of the tray going into the footwell, delivered as the punch of A's story.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then [chuckle] I had to brake.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughing] Straight into the footwell, [giggling] the whole tray.

performance_a.expected_answer: B is joining A in enjoying how ridiculous the moment was, laughing along with a story A is clearly having fun telling.

function.name: Show enjoyment
function.gloss: Laugher enjoys a pleasant incongruity and shows it. The most frequent function in the corpora.
function.framing: The trouble in the story is retold as a good story. Nothing is actually at stake; the teller is already over it and is offering the mishap up to be enjoyed.

performance_b.framing: A recounts it flatly and lands on the footwell line without lift, as if the annoyance hasn't worn off yet, so B's response has to meet a still-sore moment rather than a joke.
performance_b.laughable: Not the event — B's laugh is directed at A, marking fellow-feeling over something that still bothers A.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [flat] I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then I had to brake.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] Straight into the footwell. The whole tray.

performance_b.expected_answer: B's small laugh is a warm show of fellow-feeling toward A, softening a moment that still bothers A rather than finding it funny.

function.name: Show sympathy
function.gloss: Aligns with the interlocutor's trouble. A positive shift marked over a negative baseline.
function.framing: The trouble is real and still stings. The laugh is not at the event, it is toward the person.

why_ambiguous: The words only report what happened, never how A feels about it or how long ago it was, and neither neighbour owes the other anything, so nothing on the page settles whether B is laughing along with a good story or laughing kindly at a sore one.

pair.note: The reference pair. A mishap narrated as a good story vs. a mishap that still hurts; the responder's laugh is enjoyment vs. commiseration.

probe.open_question: You just heard a short conversation. Speaker B laughs on the line “Oh man”. What is that laugh doing — what does it convey about how B is treating what A said? Answer in one or two sentences.
probe.forced_choice_question:
You just heard a short conversation. Speaker B laughs on the line “Oh man”. Which better describes what that laugh is doing?
(a) B is joining A in enjoying how ridiculous the moment was, laughing along with a story A is clearly having fun telling.
(b) B's small laugh is a warm show of fellow-feeling toward A, softening a moment that still bothers A rather than finding it funny.
Answer with (a) or (b), then one sentence of justification.
probe.grading_note: Score the forced choice for accuracy, and the open answer against each performance's expected_answer. Report PAIR accuracy: the item counts as passed only if the model gets both performances right. Because the two performances are word-for-word identical, any model that answers from the text — or from a fixed preference for one function — scores 0 on pair accuracy, not 50%. Independent guessing scores 25%.

transcript_text:
A: I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then I had to brake.
B: And it went.
A: Straight into the footwell, the whole tray.
B: Oh man.

text_prior.note: What a strong reader guesses from the tag-free transcript alone, with no acoustic evidence. It cannot discriminate the two performances (their words are identical) — it only shows which reading is the default and how firmly it is held. `prosody_must_overturn` is the harder direction of the pair.

script_discriminability.note: Whether a reader given the performance directions recovers the intended function. Text-level proxy for the audio — confirm on the rendered audio before shipping.
